transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-05
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/records/ff-20260105-bluearc

Summary:
- Renewal and capacity discussion focused on a proposed Dedicated uplift + burst capacity for promotional spikes.
- Customer is evaluating multi-region activation (US + EU) and wants private VPC for PII workloads.
- Action items: pricing worksheet, benchmark setup, security docs.

Topics:
- Current usage and traffic patterns
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (latency, cost, isolation)
- VPC/private deployment and KMS/encryption questions
- Rollout timeline and next steps for contract amendment

Action items (quick list):
- Maya: pricing worksheet and commitment scenarios
- Ethan: perf benchmark harness and runbook
- Samira: prompt set + traffic profile

Questions raised:
- How does Redwood handle KV cache warm-up during spikes? (Liam)
- Can we get a SOC2 + encryption whitepaper and customer audit log examples? (Ravi)
- What's the fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is fully utilized? (Samira)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, just to run through the commitment scenarios and the onboarding for the eu region, um Ethan's on for any perf deck questions.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: great, thanks Maya, we only have like a short window here so if we can start with what you recommended for the 20% uplift scenario.
[00:20] Maya Chen: yep so based on last quarter you're averaging about 150 RPS at peak, with weekend promos hitting 350 RPS for short bursts, our recommended path is a small Dedicated pool for steady state plus a burst reserve to autoscale when those spikes hit, that avoids pushing everything to our hosted multi-tenant and keeps latency predictable.
[00:39] Samira Khan: quick clarifying question - when you say Dedicated pool, is that the Redwood Dedicated offering or a private on-prem option? I remember there were two names, the private one with VPC is different right?
[00:50] Ethan Morales: yeah good call — Dedicated is the reserved GPU pool we operate for you, VPC/private is a different path where the control plane is customer-managed, so there are tradeoffs. Dedicated gives you easier ops and faster time to scale; private/VPC gives you tighter network controls and residency.
[01:05] Liam O'Neill: and in terms of latency what numbers should we expect with Dedicated vs hosted? Our SLOs are 150ms p95 for inference.
[01:12] Ethan Morales: for the models you've been running we see mid-40s to 90ms p95 on Dedicated for short sequences, hosted multi-tenant can be slightly higher during noisy neighbors, especially without KV cache populated. For p95 150ms you're well within range but we'll want to run a short benchmark with your prompts to be sure.
[01:33] Ravi Patel: right, we had some noisy neighbor incidents last summer with another vendor so latency tail is a big concern. Also curious about KMS - we need bring-your-own-key.
[01:42] Maya Chen: we support customer KMS integrations, we call it KMS passthrough in the docs — we'll send the KMS whitepaper after the call. There is also HSM options for Private.
[01:53] Samira Khan: you said KV cache - I heard K-V cash earlier in the docs, how does that work with caching? We saw a big warm-up penalty on first requests.
[02:02] Ethan Morales: yeah so TTL and prefix caching are important, we do automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts, but for very long-tail sequences you'll see warm-up until the KV cache is populated. We can also kick off a bulk warm-up as part of an activation job.
[02:20] Speaker 3: (inaudible) sorry just a note, our main concern is the promotional days when traffic spikes for 10-15 minutes, we need near linear scaling with minimal cold starts.
[02:33] Maya Chen: understood, that's what the burst reserve helps with — it keeps some headroom and we have a fast ramp policy. Also we can do a short canary during a low-impact promo to validate.
[02:45] Liam O'Neill: what's the cost delta between a Dedicated pool sized for peak vs Dedicated + burst?
[02:51] Maya Chen: if you size for sustained peak it's more costly; Dedicated + burst uses a smaller committed pool plus short-term on-demand burst which is billed differently — our worksheet will show per-token and per-minute delta for the scenarios.
[03:07] Samira Khan: do you have examples of contract amendment language? Our legal usually wants precise SLA language and the fallback behavior if capacity runs out.
[03:15] Priya Rao: we can share the amendment template, and we have explicit fallback policies — automatic fallback to compatible lower-capacity model variants or to hosted with throttling. We logged this in the ops playbook last quarter.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: fallback to lower-capacity model variants — that worries our accuracy team. How does Redwood ensure quality doesn't tank?
[03:38] Ethan Morales: good point, we use model variants with similar behavior and quality profiles and we tag regressions to a prompt-set. There's a quality monitoring hook so you can get alerts if a rollouts causes a delta in eval metrics.
[03:51] Samira Khan: perfect, can we have that quality monitoring hook piped to our slack?
[03:56] Maya Chen: yes, we support Slack and webhook integrations. We'll include config examples in the runbook.
[04:05] [04:05] Liam O'Neill: about VPC, what does onboarding look like — we want our egress to stay inside our tenant and have peering with your control plane.
[04:12] Ethan Morales: for VPC there is a private control plane option — there's a short network handoff, IP allowlist, and we do a cross-account role for provisioning. Network security review usually takes 2-3 weeks depending on legal and cloud provider.
[04:27] Samira Khan: 2-3 weeks is okay; our timeline for the promo season is mid-Feb so we need this live by Feb 10 ideally. Is that feasible?
[04:34] Maya Chen: if we lock in the commitment this week and you send the prompt set, we'll prioritize the activation. The dedicated provisioning itself is typically 5 business days; VPC onboarding can be the longer path.
[04:46] Ravi Patel: what about data residency — we process EU customer PII, will traffic for those requests stay in eu?
[04:53] Priya Rao: yes, we can stage a eu-only deployment and pin model versions to eu capacity to ensure residency. We'll need to set the routing policy on your account.
[05:03] Samira Khan: okay that helps. Another question — audit logs. Our compliance team needs immutable logs for 12 months. Does Redwood retain request/response logs by default?
[05:12] Maya Chen: by default we keep logs for 90 days, but enterprise customers can get extended retention as an add-on. For PII we recommend redaction of outputs and storing hashes, and we can integrate with your SIEM. We'll send examples.
[05:27] Speaker 2: (quiet) on SOC2 how current is your report?
[05:31] Ethan Morales: our SOC2 type II is current through Q3 2025, the security pack we'll send includes the report and pen test summary.
[05:38] Liam O'Neill: sounds good. About pricing — can you walk through the commitment levels again? We want a 12-month contract but may want to start smaller and ramp at 6 months.
[05:47] Maya Chen: totally fair. We can do a stepped commitment: quarter 1 lower commit, quarter 2 upsell to full commit with a true-up. The pricing worksheet will have a stepped schedule and the per-token discounts at each tier.
[06:00] Samira Khan: any examples from other retail customers with promo spikes? I want to hear what worked and what didn't.
[06:06] Ethan Morales: sure — one retail customer used a two-pool approach: a hot Dedicated pool for latency-sensitive routes and a cheaper quantized model for long-running batch reranking. That helped reduce per-token cost while protecting latency-sensitive flows.
[06:21] Ravi Patel: quantized models — do you support 4-bit quant? Our ML team tested 4-bit but was worried about hallucinations.
[06:29] Ethan Morales: we support multiple quantization profiles, and our Optimize team can run a QC suite on your eval prompts to measure quality drop. We rarely recommend aggressive quantization for final user-facing generative text without evals.
[06:44] Samira Khan: ok - we'll send an eval set. On the benchmarks, do you need a live traffic replay or can we send synthetic traffic?
[06:52] Ethan Morales: both are fine; replay is more realistic for tail latencies, but synthetic is fine for initial headroom checks. We'll take whatever you can provide.
[06:59] Liam O'Neill: good — we'll try to provide a traffic capture from last promo.
[07:03] Maya Chen: amazing. Quick note on SLAs — the Dedicated plan includes an SLA at the contract level, we'll highlight specific uptime and latency SLOs in the amendment.
[07:14] Ravi Patel: we need to see the exact SLA language for legal.
[07:17] Maya Chen: we'll share the amendment template and highlight the SLA clauses.
[07:22] Samira Khan: thanks. On monitoring, can we get token-level cost reports broken down by route?
[07:28] Priya Rao: yes, Console supports per-route cost breakdowns, and we can set up a daily export to your S3.
[07:35] Speaker 1: (muffled) what's the expected lead time for a eu region spin-up?
[07:40] Ethan Morales: for a standard eu Dedicated node it's about 5-7 business days from commitment; if you need VPC + private control plane add the network review time.
[07:51] Samira Khan: okay. Slight tangent — competitor question: if we went with Anthropic or Cohere direct, would you say latency/cost differ materially?
[07:59] Maya Chen: it depends on model and region. We usually see Redwood Dedicated provide better price-performance for sustained workloads because of optimized runtime and batching; hosted providers sometimes have better out-of-the-box models but less predictable tails. We'll include a short benchmarking note comparing publicly available numbers.
[08:18] Liam O'Neill: perfect. Any blockers on our side to get this moving?
[08:22] Maya Chen: key things — send the prompt set, confirm desired regional footprint (US + EU), and confirm whether you want VPC or just Dedicated for now.
[08:33] Samira Khan: we'll aim to send the prompts and traffic by Jan 7. For footprint let's start with US Dedicated + EU Dedicated and revisit VPC after the benchmark.
[08:44] Priya Rao: noted. We'll scope the VPC plan as a parallel track so if you decide to move we'll have network runbook ready.
[08:51] Ravi Patel: about billing alignment — if we do stepped commitments, can you do true-ups mid-year?
[08:57] Maya Chen: yes, we support true-ups and quarter-to-quarter adjustments. We'll reflect that in the worksheet.
[09:03] [09:03] Samira Khan: last question — do you have a playground or staging endpoint for our devs to test without impacting production billing?
[09:09] Ethan Morales: yes, we can provide a sandbox project with a reduced quota for dev testing. Billing is separate per project and we can mask real data.
[09:18] Liam O'Neill: excellent.
[09:20] Maya Chen: okay, i'll recap next steps — we'll send pricing and the security pack by Jan 8, Ethan will set up the benchmark harness and share a k8s runbook by Jan 11, and Samira will share prompts/traffic by Jan 7. Is that accurate?
[09:35] Samira Khan: yes that's right.
[09:37] Ravi Patel: fine with me.
[09:39] Liam O'Neill: yep.
[09:41] Maya Chen: awesome, we'll follow up in email and i'll add the calendar for the benchmark run. Thanks everyone.
[09:47] End of meeting
